title: Canonical exceptional tensor maps under composition and etale restriction
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $X\xrightarrow{a}Y\xrightarrow{b}Z$ morphisms of arbitrary schemes. Supply $a,b,h=ba$ with open-then-proper factorizations and the ordinary unbounded etale adjunctions and tensor maps of [lem-sf-etale-ambient-adjoint-projection]. Use the canonical compact-support composition $F_h\cong F_bF_a$ [lem-etale-unbounded-compact-support-composition] and its counit-preserving right-adjoint comparison $c:G_h\cong G_aG_b$; thus $\epsilon_h$ is $\epsilon_b\circ F_b\epsilon_a$, with this comparison inserted. Suppose every $\theta_{a,P}$ is invertible. Then
$$\delta:\omega_h\xrightarrow{c_{A_Z}}G_a\omega_b\xrightarrow{\theta_{a,\omega_b}^{-1}}\omega_a\otimes_A^La^*\omega_b$$
is an isomorphism. After inserting $\delta$ and canonical pullback-tensor reassociation, the actual tensor maps satisfy
$$c_K\circ\theta_{h,K}=\theta_{a,G_bK}\circ(1_{\omega_a}\otimes a^*\theta_{b,K})\circ(\delta\otimes1_{h^*K}).$$
Consequently, if $\omega_b$ is tensor-invertible and $\theta_{b,K}$ is invertible, then $\theta_{h,K}$ is invertible. Tensor-invertible means admitting a two-sided inverse for $\otimes_A^L$.
For a separated etale $a=u$, use the normalized identification of [lem-sf-etale-unit-tensor-arbitrary-base]. The counit-preserving comparison $\lambda_P:u^*G_bP\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{bu}P$ satisfies
$$\lambda_K\circ u^*\theta_{b,K}=\theta_{bu,K}\circ(\lambda_{A_Z}\otimes1),$$
under $u^*(\omega_b\otimes b^*K)\cong u^*\omega_b\otimes(bu)^*K$. There are no Noetherian or quasi-compactness assumptions on the schemes or etale $u$ beyond the supplied factorizations. These are equations of canonical derived morphisms, not only isomorphisms of endpoints.

source.place: Paragraph 3, transposing the projection map and composite counits. Generic non-smooth transitivity underlying upstream SmoothDuality/Local.lean lines 239-319; compare lem-asd-tensor-mate-etale-precomp, whose current statement only permits Noetherian schemes. Includes the actual etale restriction equation needed to descend the tensor morphism.

proof.text:
Write $\otimes=\otimes_A^L$, $W=\omega_a$, $V=\omega_b$ and $Q=b^*K$. Use [lem-sf-etale-compact-projection-coherence] to normalize the compact-support comparison $E:F_h\cong F_bF_a$ and to obtain the natural inverse projections $q_f$. In the calculation identify $F_h$ with $F_bF_a$ using $E$, and $G_h$ with $G_aG_b$ using the specified counit-preserving $c$. This is notation for conjugating every map by these comparisons. Thus the composite counit is exactly that of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. The canonical pullback tensor comparison [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] is inserted throughout. By the definition in [lem-sf-etale-ambient-adjoint-projection], put
$$\phi_f(P)=(\epsilon_{f,A}\otimes1_P)\circ q_f(\omega_f,P):F_f(\omega_f\otimes f^*P)\to P.$$
Its adjunct is $\theta_{f,P}$. Unit constraints are those of [lem-kun-tensor-unit].

source.place: Paragraph 3: fix the projection and composite-counit normalizations before transposing.

proof.text:
Set $M=W\otimes a^*V$, $s=\theta_{a,V}:M\to G_aV$ and $d=c_{A_Z}^{-1}\circ s:M\to\omega_h$. By hypothesis $s$ is invertible, hence $d=\delta^{-1}$ is invertible. Put $v=\phi_a(V):F_aM\to V$. The defining transpose of $s$ is $\epsilon_{a,V}\circ F_a(s)=v$ [lem-sf-etale-ambient-adjoint-projection]. Therefore the composite counit [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], with $c_{A_Z}\circ d=s$, gives the actual equality
$$\epsilon_{h,A_Z}\circ F_h(d)=\epsilon_{b,A_Z}\circ F_b(v):F_hM\to A_Z.$$
This proves the first isomorphism assertion and records the scalar counit needed below.

source.place: Paragraph 3: scalar component of the composite-counit calculation.

proof.text:
Identify $D=M\otimes a^*Q$ with $W\otimes a^*(V\otimes Q)$ by the tensor comparison. The defining adjunct formula and naturality of $q_a$ imply naturality of $\theta_a$: for $t:P\to P'$, the transposes of $G_a(t)\circ\theta_{a,P}$ and $\theta_{a,P'}\circ(1_W\otimes a^*t)$ both equal $t\circ\phi_a(P)$, by counit naturality. Apply this with $t=\theta_{b,K}:V\otimes Q\to G_bK$. The composite-adjunction transpose of
$$R=\theta_{a,G_bK}\circ(1_W\otimes a^*\theta_{b,K}):D\to G_aG_bK$$
is consequently
$$T_R=\phi_b(K)\circ F_b(\phi_a(V\otimes Q)).$$
Here the two Hom bijections are exactly those in [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], and the identities for $\phi$ are their defining transposes, rather than any assertion about isomorphic endpoints.

source.place: Paragraph 3: transpose the iterated tensor map, explicitly using naturality.

proof.text:
The tensor-associativity identity of [lem-sf-etale-compact-projection-coherence] at $(W,V,Q)$ says
$$q_a(W,V\otimes Q)=(q_a(W,V)\otimes1_Q)\circ q_a(M,Q).$$
Postcompose with $\epsilon_{a,A_Y}\otimes1_V\otimes1_Q$. The definition of $v$ in step 2 gives
$$\phi_a(V\otimes Q)=(v\otimes1_Q)\circ q_a(M,Q).$$
Substitute this into step 3 and use $\phi_b(K)=(\epsilon_{b,A_Z}\otimes1_K)\circ q_b(V,K)$. Naturality of $q_b$ at $v:F_aM\to V$ gives
$$T_R=((\epsilon_{b,A_Z}\circ F_bv)\otimes1_K)\circ q_b(F_aM,K)\circ F_b(q_a(M,Q)).$$
All displayed sources are $F_bF_aD$ and targets are $K$; associators are the fixed ones of step 1.

source.place: Paragraph 3: expand the two tensor reassociations using projection associativity.

proof.text:
The composition equation of [lem-sf-etale-compact-projection-coherence], with $E$ inserted as in step 1, replaces $q_b(F_aM,K)\circ F_b(q_a(M,Q))$ in step 4 by $q_h(M,K)$. Thus
$$T_R=((\epsilon_{b,A_Z}\circ F_bv)\otimes1_K)\circ q_h(M,K).$$
For $L=c_K\circ\theta_{h,K}\circ(d\otimes1_{h^*K}):D\to G_aG_bK$, the defining transpose of $\theta_h$ [lem-sf-etale-ambient-adjoint-projection] and naturality of $q_h$ at $d$ instead give
$$T_L=((\epsilon_{h,A_Z}\circ F_hd)\otimes1_K)\circ q_h(M,K).$$
Step 2 identifies the bracketed counits, so $T_L=T_R$. Injectivity of the composite Hom bijection [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] gives $L=R$. Precompose with $\delta\otimes1$ and restore the comparisons to obtain exactly
$$c_K\circ\theta_{h,K}=\theta_{a,G_bK}\circ(1_W\otimes a^*\theta_{b,K})\circ(\delta\otimes1_{h^*K}).$$

source.place: Paragraph 3: compare both actual transposes and use the adjunction bijection.

proof.text: In the equation of step 5, $c_K$ and $\delta$ are isomorphisms, $\theta_{a,G_bK}$ is an isomorphism by the hypothesis for every $P$, and $1_W\otimes a^*\theta_{b,K}$ is an isomorphism whenever $\theta_{b,K}$ is: apply the pullback and tensor functors to its inverse. Hence $\theta_{h,K}$ is invertible. This proves the stated consequence when $\omega_b$ is tensor-invertible; that extra hypothesis is actually unnecessary for this consequence under the given universal hypothesis on $\theta_a$.

source.place: Paragraph 3: invertibility follows from the equality of canonical maps.

proof.text:
Now take $a=u$ separated etale. Write $\rho_P:G_uP\xrightarrow{\sim}u^*P$ and $\eta:\omega_u\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X$ for the normalized maps of [lem-sf-etale-unit-tensor-arbitrary-base]. It gives both the hypothesis on every $\theta_u$ and the equation $\rho_P\theta_{u,P}=\ell_{u^*P}(\eta\otimes1)$, where $\ell$ denotes the left unit constraint [lem-kun-tensor-unit] (written $\lambda$ in that node; here $\lambda$ is reserved for the comparison below). The counit-preserving comparison in the question is
$$\lambda_P=c_P^{-1}\circ\rho_{G_bP}^{-1}:u^*G_bP\to G_{bu}P.$$
Indeed it is the same composite Hom bijection with $G_u$ replaced by $u^*$ through its counit-preserving normalization [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. At $P=A_Z$, the definition of $\delta$ and the normalization of $\theta_{u,V}$ give
$$\lambda_{A_Z}^{-1}=\rho_V\circ c_{A_Z}=\ell_{u^*V}\circ(\eta\otimes1)\circ\delta.$$

source.place: Paragraph 3: identify the etale right adjoint by its evaluation counit, including its scalar component.

proof.text:
Apply $\rho_{G_bK}$ to step 5 for $(u,b)$. The normalization in [lem-sf-etale-unit-tensor-arbitrary-base], and naturality of the tensor unit constraints [lem-kun-tensor-unit], turn its right side into
$$u^*\theta_{b,K}\circ(\lambda_{A_Z}^{-1}\otimes1).$$
The left side is $\lambda_K^{-1}\circ\theta_{bu,K}$ by step 7. Multiplying by $\lambda_K$ on the left and by $\lambda_{A_Z}\otimes1$ on the right proves
$$\lambda_K\circ u^*\theta_{b,K}=\theta_{bu,K}\circ(\lambda_{A_Z}\otimes1).$$
The canonical source identification is [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal]. Every input above is an arbitrary object of the ordinary unbounded etale derived category. All factorizations were supplied, and no step uses a compactification existence theorem, quasi-compactness, Noetherianity, purity, or a change of coefficient category.

source.place: Paragraph 3: cancel the normalized etale tensor unit and recover the restriction equation.
